lessons.title: Small Choices, Huge Results
lessons.key_idea: Small actions repeated consistently over time compound into dramatic results, just as a penny doubled every day eventually outgrows a million dollars.

lessons.title: You Are Fully Responsible
lessons.key_idea: Your life is the sum of your choices, so taking complete ownership of your results is the first step to changing them.

lessons.title: Track Everything You Want to Change
lessons.key_idea: Writing down your daily behavior, such as every dollar spent or every bite eaten, reveals the unconscious habits steering your life.

lessons.title: Find Your Why to Change Habits
lessons.key_idea: Lasting habit change comes from a compelling personal reason, which gives you the willpower to remove bad habits and build good ones.

lessons.title: Routines Build Unstoppable Momentum
lessons.key_idea: Starting is the hardest part, but steady routines and rhythm create momentum that makes progress feel almost effortless.

lessons.title: Guard Your Inputs and Influences
lessons.key_idea: What you read, watch and listen to, the people you spend time with, and your environment all quietly push you toward or away from your goals.

lessons.title: Go Beyond Expectations to Accelerate
lessons.key_idea: Doing a little more than expected at key moments, then staying consistent, multiplies the compound effect and ties every lesson together.

plan.title: The Compound Effect
plan.author: Darren Hardy
plan.confidence_note: I know the book's core framework, chapter structure and main examples well, though I may not recall every minor anecdote or exact wording.
plan.one_liner: Tiny, boring choices repeated daily quietly add up to massive success or slow failure.
plan.summary: Darren Hardy, former publisher of Success magazine, argues there is no secret to achievement. Results come from small, smart choices made consistently over a long time. The trouble is that these choices feel insignificant in the moment, so we skip the good ones and indulge the bad ones without noticing the cost. Hardy shows how to take full responsibility for your life, track your daily behavior, and replace bad habits with good ones by connecting them to a deeper reason. He explains how routines create momentum that becomes hard to stop, and how the people, information and surroundings you allow in shape your direction. Finally, he urges readers to go beyond what is expected at key moments to accelerate results. The book is a practical case for patience, consistency and personal ownership.
